title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-07
source: flac16/48kHz; 7 Inch Half Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips(Recorded In Venue By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel 2 Reel)- 1st Generation Cassettes (TDK SA-X 100's) Taped By Dick Latvala(Technics 1506 Reel 2 Reel-Tascam 122 MK111 Cassette Deck no dolby); Analog to Digital Transfer(Dick's Cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon- Sony PCM-R500 DAT @ 44.1KHz by Jim Wise circa 1997); DAT play back on a Sony PCM R-500-Analog out-Sony PCM R-700 Analog in @ 48KHz-Digital Audio Labs Carddeluxe-WAV @ 16/48kHz; Editing(Adobe Audition 3.0)-Mastering(iZotope Ozone 6)-FLAC Encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name)

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear audience recording of a rare 1970 show that dazzles with acoustic opening, cosmic second set and a stellar Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the pristine Bear/Wise tape – it sounds “crystal clear,” “beautiful,” and like hearing the concert for the first time. The performance is praised for its acoustic opener, the space‑filled second set and especially the Other One/cryptic reprise stretch, though a few note that the band wasn’t always razor‑sharp. Overall the show is considered a gem of 1970‑era Dead magic.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews (12 out of 15) give 5‑star praise for both sound quality and performance, with only one modest 3‑star comment about playing. Recording is rated excellent; show quality is good‑to‑great, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers describe the tape as crystal clear, beautiful, crisp and superbly transferred. No complaints about hiss, drop‑outs or balance.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic numbers open the first set, then the band launches into a cosmic second‑set that includes a highlight‑filled Other One sequence and a memorable Cryptical reprise; some listeners felt the electric portion was a bit unfocused but overall it flows well.

band_member_comments.Drums: Jim F notes the drummers lock in and drive the intense moments, especially during the Other One stretch.
